JOINT APPLICATION OF ONCOR       §

LLC AND LCRA TSC TO AMEND        §
THEIR CERTIFICATES OF            §
                                          BEFORE THE STATE OFFICE
CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY FOR    §
THE BELL COUNTY EAST SWITCH      §
TO BIG HILL SUBSTATION 765-KV    §
TRANSMISSION LINE PROJECT IN     §                  OF
BELL, BURNET, CONCHO, CORYELL,   §
LAMPASAS, LLANO, MASON,          §
MCCULLOCH, MENARD, MILAM,        §    ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS
MILLS, SAN SABA, SCHLEICHER,     §
TOM GREEN, AND WILLIAMSON        §
COUNTIES                         §




                       DIRECT TESTIMONY

                                 OF

                         SCOTT HOUSTON




                           MAY 10, 2026
  1   I.     INTRODUCTION

 2   Q.     Please state your name and address.
3    A.     My name is Scott Houston. I am the landowner at 509 Cloudwood Ranch Road, Briggs,
4           Texas 78608 address adjacent to the G2 Line.

 5   Q.     Who owns your property?
 6   A.     Scott and Leslie Houston.

 7   Q.     What is the physical address of your property?
 8   A.     509 Cloudwood Ranch Road, Briggs, Texas 78608

 9   Q.     On whose behalf are you testifying?

10   A.     I am testifying on my own behalf.


11   II.    PURPOSE OF TESTIMONY

12   Q.     What is the purpose of your testimony in this proceeding?
13   A.     I am opposed to using the G2 Line for the proposed transmission line.


14   III.   TESTIMONY

15   Q.     What is your overall concern with the proposed routing adjacent to your property?
16   A.     Property values are a concern, but not so much for me because I don’t plan to ever move
17          from this house. The view and environmental concern are my main issue.

18   Q.     Which routes affect your property?
19   A.     My property is affected by routes 266, 295, 296, 304, 322, 366, 376, 381, 382, 524, 527,
20          535, 543, 546, 547, 548, 551, 557, 572, 580, 582, 668, 706, 729, 739, 900, and 905.

21   Q.     What routes do you oppose or support?
22   A.     I oppose the construction of all routes utilizing the G2 link and the G6 link, to include
23          routes 266, 295, 296, 304, 322, 366, 376, 381, 382, 524, 527, 535, 543, 546, 547, 548, 551,
24          557, 572, 580, 582, 668, 706, 729, 739, 900, and 905.

25   Q.     Are there any habitable structures on your property, and if so, how many?
26   A.     Yes, one.



                                                     2
  1   Q.    Please describe these habitable structures and their proximity to the proposed
 2   transmission line.
 3   A.     Our single-family residential home is approximately 2,400 square feet and located around
 4          one mile from the proposed G2 line.

 5   Q.    Are you concerned about the effect of the proposed transmission line on your
 6   habitable structures, and if so, how and why?
 7   A.     the G2 Line is selected, the transmission towers would likely be visible from my home,
 8          decreasing its value. Public studies raise concerns about the potential health risks of living
 9          in close proximity to high voltage lines. I am most concerned that the constant hum of the
10          lines will be audible from my home, further decreasing the number of potential buyers who
11          would even consider purchasing the property in the future.

12   Q.     Are there unique physical features near your property that you believe make
13   construction of the proposed transmission line difficult, and if so, what are they and why?
14   A.     Yes. The proposed G2 Line runs in close proximity to a rocket test facility and underground
15          gas pipeline. The proposed line runs adjacent to Firefly’s Rocket Ranch facility, which
16          recently experienced a large fireball explosion from a rocket booster malfunction on
17          September 29th, 2025. In addition, there is one existing gas pipeline and a plan for a second
18          that runs in front of the Firefly facility, creating a concentration of industrial infrastructure.
19          Burnet County is often in a burn ban due to dry weather conditions, and our local fire
20          station is completely volunteer and understaffed. This could limit the speed and scale of
21          the response to a large-scale industrial or an electrical emergency. This same fire station,
22          Northeast Burnet County Emergency Services District Fire Station #2, has an active
23          helipad used for Care Flight operations. There is a significant concern that the transmission
24          lines on the G2 Line could interfere with emergency flight paths or operations. Assistant
25          Chief Clayton Potter stated great concern that combining high-voltage transmission lines
26          with rocket testing and gas pipelines creates an escalated threat to the citizens and property
27          of Briggs.

28   Q.    What do you believe would be the environmental impact of the proposed
29   transmission line near your property?
30   A.     I manage my property under a songbird wildlife management tax exemption. One
31          requirement is to provide a safe habitat through various means. Large power lines create
32          a collusion risk, the construction modifies the habitat, and – most importantly, the
33          noise/electromagnetic field created by such lines may disrupt songbirds. In fact, some
34          studies suggest migratory birds that use Earth’s magnetic field for navigation could
35          experience localized disruption near strong electromagnetic sources.
36
37   Q.    Do you believe that the proposed transmission line is against the community values
38   you hold regarding your property and the area of Texas where your property is located?
39          Yes. The proposed 765 kV transmission towers are among the tallest structures in the utility
40          1 world. They would break the “big sky” horizon and dominate the view, turning a natural


                                                        3
 1          and peaceful setting into an industrial corridor. Clearing a 200-foot-wide swath of native
2          vegetation for the proposed transmission lines could fragment habitats and disrupt the
3          migratory patterns of local wildlife, as mentioned above.

 4   Q.    In addition to opposing the G2 Line, are there any other lines you oppose?
 5   A.    I oppose the G6 Line as well as the G13 Line.

 6   Q.    Why do you oppose these lines?
 7   A.    These lines make it possible for G2 to be implemented, which would then place the
 8         transmission lines near Firefly Rocket Ranch and the gas pipeline that runs adjacent to
 9         Firefly.

10   Q.    Do you have any photographs or drawings that you believe would assist the
11         commission in understanding your testimony, and if so, please describe and attach
12         them?
13   A.    Yes, this is my view towards where the proposed lines could be located. It is currently
14         unobstructed, and I’d like it to stay that way.




15

16   IV.   CONCLUSION

17   Q.    Does this conclude your testimony at this time?
18   A.    Yes, it does.
